checked_sources.source: Haddouche & Sakhi 2026 v2, Appendix C Theorem C.1 and proof
checked_sources.result: Primary-verified a stronger off-policy past-dependent-prior result than the main-text fixed-prior theorem, but for a different target. Under arbitrarily evolving context distributions, Q_k may depend on data through time k, and the time-uniform cumulative bound uses the product prior Q_0 tensor ... tensor Q_{K-1}, yielding the exact complexity sum_k KL(Q_k||Q_{k-1}). The proof explicitly relies on Q_{K-1} being F_{K-1}-measurable, conditional Fubini, a nonnegative martingale and Ville's inequality. The algorithm uses only the current batch plus the previous posterior/policy because older raw data may be stale under arbitrary drift.

checked_sources.source: Shin, Ramdas, Rinaldo, E-detectors: a nonparametric framework for sequential change detection, arXiv:2203.03532 / NEJSDS
checked_sources.result: Primary-verified a nonparametric sequential change-detection framework built from e-processes. It gives nonasymptotic average-run-length false-alarm control in broad composite settings and near-optimal detection-delay rates in sub-Gaussian/sub-exponential cases, including bounded-mean changes without iid assumptions. Predictable mixtures of valid baseline increments retain validity.

candidates_new.mechanism: When the data-generating context distribution may drift arbitrarily, stop treating all historical raw observations as equally current. Learn Q_k from the current batch while using Q_{k-1} as the reference distribution, and pay cumulative local change complexity sum KL(Q_k||Q_{k-1}) rather than distance to a single ancient prior.
primary_sources: Haddouche & Sakhi 2026 v2, Appendix C Theorem C.1
candidates_new.quantitative_or_formal_evidence: With probability at least 1-delta, for every horizon K the average sequential risk is bounded by average current-batch logarithmic-smoothing empirical risk plus [sum_{k=0}^K KL(Q_k||Q_{k-1}) + log(1/delta)]/[lambda (K+1)m]. The proof constructs P^K=Q_0 tensor ... tensor Q_{K-1}, uses F_{K-1}-measurability and Ville's inequality, so the previous posterior is a directly verified off-policy reference in this dynamic cumulative-risk setting.
candidates_new.scope: Time-varying context distributions, current-batch conditional independence, bounded costs and the paper's LS/off-policy policy representation. The guarantee targets average sequential risk across changing environments, not the stationary single-policy global-history objective of Theorem 3.2.
candidates_new.failure_conditions: Using only current data wastes useful old evidence when the regime is actually stable. Small local KL steps can accumulate into large long-run drift. The result does not itself detect when to switch between stable/global-history and drifting/local-history modes, and it does not certify one final stationary policy after arbitrary drift.
candidates_new.transfer_hypothesis: Maintain two formally distinct evidence modes: stable mode reuses global history under the fixed-prior all-k/all-Q theorem; drift mode uses current evidence plus previous-posterior continuity under Theorem C.1. Never mix their guarantees. A separate sequential change detector decides when evidence is stale enough to enter drift mode.
candidates_new.confidence: high for source theorem; medium for two-mode scheduler transfer

candidates_new.mechanism: Run an anytime nonparametric e-detector on a compact stream of environment/performance diagnostics. While the no-change hypothesis remains credible, retain long-history evidence; after a statistically controlled change alarm, restart or shorten raw-data memory and switch to the local previous-posterior update regime.
candidates_new.quantitative_or_formal_evidence: E-detectors provide nonasymptotic false-alarm average-run-length control for composite nonparametric pre-change classes and near-optimal detection-delay rates in sub-Gaussian/sub-exponential settings. The off-policy Appendix C theorem separately certifies local current-batch learning with cumulative KL path cost under arbitrary context evolution.
candidates_new.scope: The change detector and learner are separately certified components. The e-detector requires a well-defined monitored null/statistic; the off-policy learner requires its own propensity/support and cost assumptions.
candidates_new.failure_conditions: No end-to-end theorem was found for the combined switch. Slow drift may not trigger quickly; noisy alarms can cause unnecessary forgetting; the monitored diagnostic may miss semantically important distribution change; detector reset semantics can interact with repeated/recurring regimes.
candidates_new.transfer_hypothesis: Use a small, independent drift evidence channel to decide evidence half-life: stable => global accumulation; alarm => current-batch/local-posterior mode; after re-stabilization => begin a fresh global-history lineage. Preserve detector evidence, learning evidence and hard safety constraints as separate layers.
candidates_new.confidence: high for component theorems; medium-low for composed optimizer architecture

evidence_updates.update: The off-policy picture is now split more precisely. Main-text Theorem 3.2 keeps a data-independent fixed prior for stationary global-history reuse, but Appendix C Theorem C.1 directly uses previous posteriors Q_{k-1} as predictable reference distributions and proves a time-uniform cumulative-risk bound under arbitrary context drift. Thus 'predictable prior in off-policy learning' is verified in the local/dynamic objective, while the stationary all-history/all-Q predictable-prior extension remains open.

Primary proof inspection confirms the cumulative KL path term is not merely a heuristic regularizer: it arises exactly as KL(Q^K||P^K)=sum KL(Q_k||Q_{k-1}) with P^K built from past posteriors, and the exponential mixture is a nonnegative martingale because each Q_{k-1} is F_{k-1}-measurable.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: One predictable-prior theorem can simultaneously give full-history stationary reuse, arbitrary-drift robustness, and one final-policy certificate.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: Not established. The verified theorems separate these objectives: main Theorem 3.2 reuses all data with fixed P under stationary contexts; Appendix C uses current batch plus Q_{k-1} and controls average sequential risk under arbitrary context evolution.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.reason: Keep stable and drift modes as separate lineages until a unified theorem is found.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: An e-detector alarm automatically validates discarding old off-policy evidence and switching learners.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: Not established. E-detectors certify false-alarm/delay properties for the monitored change hypothesis, not downstream policy-risk optimality after a switch.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.reason: Treat drift detection as a routing signal whose false-alarm/delay guarantee is separate from the learning certificates before and after the switch.

frontier: Search for a unified stationary sequential off-policy PAC-Bayes theorem that allows an F_{k-1}-measurable learned prior while still reusing all historical batches and retaining simultaneous all-k/all-Q certification. Compare its proof obstacle with Appendix C's product-prior construction.

Specify a practical e-detector statistic for evidence staleness that is independent of the optimizer's candidate-selection score; test abrupt, gradual and recurring drift and quantify false-memory-reset versus stale-memory costs.
Formalize restart semantics after drift: what prior mass and historical evidence may be carried into a fresh stable lineage without double-using the alarm-triggering data?
Complete the frozen vector off-policy reduction and compare joint vector CS geometry with scalar alpha splitting on correlated objectives.
Extend atomic deterministic certificates to a countable description-length prior and define safe admission of configs not in the original support.
Continue heavy-tail support: robustify the detector and off-policy score layers separately before attempting any combined guarantee.

actions_taken_instead_of_stopping: Inspected Appendix C's full proof after the first checkpoint and found a direct off-policy previous-posterior construction that materially refined the earlier frontier.
Separated stationary global-history and arbitrary-drift local-history guarantees instead of collapsing them into one claim.
Added nonparametric anytime change detection as a distinct routing component, while explicitly refusing to transfer its guarantee to downstream policy risk.

exact_next_action: Compare the fixed-prior supermartingale proof of Theorem 3.2 with Appendix C's product-prior martingale line by line to determine whether a predictable prior can coexist with full-history reuse without double counting. Then design the smallest independently monitored e-detector statistic that can route stable/global-history versus drift/local-history evidence while keeping the switch itself outside both learning certificates.
